mappings.applicability_reason: This requirement's applicable conditions are 'customer content is sent to an external model provider' and 'the content sent includes restricted data.' The tuning job (cmp-003) fine-tunes the vendor's base model (cmp-008) on the training store's contents (evd-002), but whether this fine-tuning computation executes within the pipeline's own environment or on vendor infrastructure is not established (evd-002), so whether customer content is actually transmitted to the vendor is conditional on that unresolved fact rather than settled by the documentation.
assumptions: Assumes that if fine-tuning executes on vendor infrastructure, the data made available to it is the training store's contents as described in evd-003, since no separate minimization step for the tuning job itself is documented.

mappings.applicability_reason: This requirement applies where customer data is sent to an external provider that processes it on the system's behalf. The vendor (act-003) supplies the base model the tuning job fine-tunes (evd-002), but the documentation does not establish whether the fine-tuning computation itself runs on vendor infrastructure -- which would make the vendor a processor of transcript data -- or entirely within the pipeline's own environment, so applicability turns on this unresolved fact.

The training corpus derives from customer ticket transcripts (evd-002, evd-003), so this requirement's applicable condition holds, and the non-applicable condition ('synthetic, public, or contains no sensitive elements') does not, since the corpus contains names, email addresses, and message bodies. This applies regardless of where fine-tuning execution occurs, because the minimization question concerns what enters the training corpus, not where the corpus is later consumed.

The training store holds PII (evd-002, evd-003), satisfying the applicable condition that the system stores confidential or restricted data; and this threat's specific concern -- transcript data crossing a network boundary to vendor infrastructure -- would additionally trigger the 'data crosses a network boundary the system does not control' condition if execution is vendor-side.

documentation_gaps.title: Fine-tuning execution location and any resulting vendor data exposure are not documented
documentation_gaps.description: The system overview describes the tuning job as fine-tuning the vendor's base model on the training store's current contents (evd-002), but does not state whether that computation executes within the pipeline's own environment or on the vendor's infrastructure, nor -- if the latter -- what data would cross that boundary, in what form, or under what vendor retention or usage terms.
documentation_gaps.importance: This fact governs whether several requirements (external-provider data minimization, external processor data handling disclosure, encryption across an uncontrolled network boundary) are actually engaged, and whether unredacted customer PII -- names, email addresses, and full message bodies (evd-003) -- reaches the vendor. Without it, the disclosure risk this threat describes can be neither confirmed nor ruled out.
requested_evidence: A statement of where the tuning job's fine-tuning computation executes (within the pipeline's own environment versus a vendor-hosted service)
If vendor-hosted, a description of what data is transmitted to the vendor and any contractual retention or usage terms governing it
Confirmation of whether any data transmitted to the vendor is encrypted in transit
